author: WP13
summary: Updated chapter on cna_tool_gltf_to_cnj, the per-type version-2 Model envelope, sidecar validation, offline/runtime parity, the dual-texture occlusion remap and route choice. Mostly current; TARGET differs in that the conversion is shared with cna-content and gltf_to_cnb, unknown strides are refused, morph sidecars are strictly validated with a tangent trailer, cameras are not carried in CNJ, and the dual-texture route is reached only by unlit materials. Tutorial 111 had the user workflow; reader rules, sidecar edges, parity tests and the remap derivation now live on the CNJ toolchain deep dive.

concepts.text: Direct runtime glTF keeps all scene groups in one Model but fixes unit scale at 1; cna_tool_gltf_to_cnj runs the same import core and packing, then writes each group as CNJ plus binary sidecars.
The converter is the reproducible path for controlled scaling, one-output-per-group packaging and inspectable, committable artefacts.
cmake/ToolGltfToCnj.cmake builds the tool unconditionally (not behind CNA_BUILD_TESTS) and links CNA plus sharp-runtime components.
The tool never initialises a window, graphics device or renderer; it only constructs math value types.
tokens: never initialises a window, a graphics device or a renderer

concepts.text: The tool also compiles the test-scope GltfOracleEXT.cpp for its --dump-oracle mode and links the Draco decoder for that mode in Draco builds.
Command line: cna_tool_gltf_to_cnj input.gltf|glb outputDir baseName [unitScale]; unitScale must be a positive number; errors print error: and exit 1; the output directory is created.
The same conversion is compiled into cna_content as ConvertGltfToCnj and used by cna-content and cna_tool_gltf_to_cnb before compiling to .cnb.
concepts.note: New at TARGET relative to the claim's single tool.

concepts.text: Per group the tool writes <name>.cnj (version-2 Model), <name>_meshN_verts.bin and _idx.bin, optional _morph.bin, optional <name>.skeleton.bin, one version-1 AnimationClip CNJ per clip and extracted textures with stable suffixes.
Rigid scene-node clips are also written as AnimationClip CNJ documents carrying their target space.
concepts.note: The claim listed clips for skinned groups only.

concepts.text: Textures are written once per source image; an occlusion image rewritten for the dual-texture convention is written as a separate _texoccN.png.
Multiple groups get _static or skin-name suffixes; colliding sanitized names are refused; runtime and offline keep the same group set but package it differently.
Sidecar paths in a Model .cnj are bare names resolved against the ContentManager root, not the descriptor's folder.
Every CNJ carries cnjVersion and type; the version ceiling is per type: Model's maximum is 2, all others 1, so raising Model's ceiling blesses no other type.
Version 2 adds a bones array (name, parent, 16-float local transform, parent-before-child, identity root at 0) and a per-mesh parentBone, preserving glTF hierarchy and rigid instancing placement.

Version 2 additively carries the import report, rigid clips, material-variant names and per-variant entries, topology, UV selectors and transforms, newer PBR fields, partOfMesh grouping and the flat-normal morph flag.
concepts.note: Extends the claim's list with TARGET fields (partOfMesh, flat-normal flag, specular, unlit).

concepts.text: Claim that the version-2 envelope carries cameras: gltf_to_cnj writes no cameras, only the report's camera-node count, so cameras exist on direct glTF loads alone.
tokens: It does not carry imported cameras
concepts.note: Contradicts the claim; the corrected statement is on the page.

target.evidence: tools/gltf_to_cnj/gltf_to_cnj.cpp (no camera array; cameraNodeCount only); modules/content/src/Xna/ContentManager.cpp (setCamerasEXTProperty only in ReadGltfModel)

concepts.text: The reader supplies empty or glTF-default carriers for fields older Model documents lack.
The reader always builds entry 0 as root and does not apply its serialized transform or parent.
tokens: its serialized transform and parent are not applied

concepts.text: Later parents are bounds-checked (out-of-range is a ContentLoadException) but parent < child is not required; a forward parent builds a pointer tree whose CopyAbsoluteBoneTransformsTo order is wrong.
A transform array with any count other than 16 silently becomes identity.
A mesh parentBone out of range is a ContentLoadException.
tokens: a mesh parentBone out of range

concepts.text: Generated files satisfy these rules; a hand-edited version-2 descriptor can load into an inconsistent graph rather than fail at the schema boundary.
Version-1 Model files remain loadable; without a hierarchy the reader builds Root plus one named child bone per mesh, which lets ported samples find part bones by name.
Vertex and index bytes use the packed stride ABI; the descriptor supplies vertexStride (default 16) and paths; counts are derived from file sizes; 32-bit indices when vertices exceed 65,535.
A non-positive stride silently skips the mesh entry.
tokens: a stride of zero or less silently skips that mesh entry

concepts.text: Claim that an unknown positive stride can produce an unfilled vertex buffer: it is refused with a ContentLoadException naming the stride.
tokens: refused with a ContentLoadException naming the stride

concepts.text: Vertex and index byte lengths not divisible by the element size are truncated by integer division rather than rejected.
Morph sidecars are read strictly: target counts, per-target vertex counts, normal/tangent flags, an optional versioned tangent trailer and leftover bytes are all validated.
concepts.note: Stricter than the claim described; the tangent trailer is new.

concepts.text: What remains trusted is the semantic agreement between descriptor and sidecars.
tokens: semantic agreement between the descriptor and its sidecars

concepts.text: The skeleton sidecar's bone count must lie in 0..100,000 before allocation; it holds bind poses and inverse binds, and version 2 may append a SkeletonRootPrefix block.

The third block is read only when at least boneCount*64 bytes remain, otherwise identity; a partial trailing fragment is ignored and extra bytes after a complete block are not required to be consumed.
tokens: cannot distinguish a genuinely old file from a partially written new one

concepts.text: Appending an optional fixed-size block instead of changing the first two keeps old sidecars valid; producers should publish sidecars atomically.
Clip CNJs referenced by a Model go through the manager's cached Load<AnimationClipEXT>, so models can share one clip object.
Mesh buffers, stock effects and most graph objects are created per described part and retained by the private ownership bundle; a palette clip on a skeleton-less model is skipped with a warning.
Sharing GltfImportCore reduces drift but does not prove parity, because the front ends do different work after extraction.
tokens: does not prove parity by itself

concepts.text: The parity contract is not byte identity between JSON and a live object but equal placement, palette spaces, vertex/index bytes, material state and animation records for the same group.
tokens: The contract is not byte identity

concepts.text: A fix made in only one front end is a regression even if the shared parser still builds.
tokens: A fix made in only one front end is a regression

concepts.text: GltfToCnjToolTests spawns the real converter as a process (excluded on Windows, Emscripten, Android and iOS) and compares skinning data, animation clips, L6 material state, morphed flat normals and diagnostics across both routes.
glTF occlusion uses 1.0 for full light, while DualTextureEffect doubles its second texture, so 0.5 is neutral and passing glTF's image unchanged brightens.
RemapOcclusionImageForDualTextureEXT decodes the image, halves RGB (alpha unchanged) and re-encodes PNG: o_dual = o_gltf / 2.
The halving is integer division, so white becomes 127 and neutral lands at 254/255 — a sub-percent darkening.
The remapped image is cached separately because the same source may also feed an unmodified PbrEffect occlusion map.
Runtime and converter share the one remap; tests cover successful remapping and refusal of undecodable bytes.
At TARGET only an unskinned, uncoloured, unlit primitive with base-colour and occlusion maps reaches DualTextureEffect; ordinary metallic-roughness materials use PbrEffect's real occlusion map.
concepts.note: The dual-texture route became much narrower after the material-model rule.

concepts.text: Use direct glTF for files in metres whatever their group count; the converter for unit conversion, per-group assets or reviewed bytes; .xnb when an XNA pipeline governs; the legacy path only for SkinnedModelEXT.
tokens: whether it holds one group or several
concepts.note: The claim advised direct glTF only for single-group files; runtime now keeps every group.

concepts.text: A converted .cnj can be compiled to .cnb with cna_tool_cnj_to_cnb, or glTF compiled straight to .cnb with cna_tool_gltf_to_cnb --unit-scale.
concepts.note: Adds the .cnb routes available at TARGET.

concepts.text: Do not hand-edit counts or offsets in a generated Model CNJ without regenerating or validating the sidecars; JSON and binaries form one asset contract.

examples.text: cna_tool_gltf_to_cnj input.gltf outputDir baseName [unitScale] command line
examples.note: Usage text and argument checks read in tools/gltf_to_cnj/gltf_to_cnj.cpp main(); not executed.

issues.text: The .cnj Model reader silently skips a mesh entry whose vertexStride is zero or negative instead of refusing the descriptor.
.cnj vertex/index sidecar sizes that are not whole multiples of the stride or index size are truncated by integer division rather than rejected.
The .cnj bones parser accepts a forward parent (parent >= child) and turns a transform array of the wrong length into identity, producing an inconsistent graph instead of a load error.
The skeleton sidecar's optional third (root-prefix) block is detected by remaining size, so a truncated partial block is ignored; a compatibility design choice.
An unknown positive vertexStride in a .cnj no longer yields an unfilled vertex buffer; it is refused (GLTF-157).
The CNJ Model route carries no imported cameras (only the camera-node count in the import report).
